title: The critical one-half conjecture for circle packings
statement:
Let $4\mathcal{S}4$ be a circle packing and let $s_0\in\mathcal{S}$. For $0<p<1$, let $E_{\mathcal{S},p}(s_0,r)$ denote the event that $s_0$ is connected to distance $r$ by open disks, and let $E_{\mathcal{S},p}(s_0,\infty)$ denote the event that it is connected to infinity. **The critical one-half conjecture for circle packings.**

$$
\mathbb{P}(E_{\mathcal{S},1/2}(s_0,\infty))=0.
$$

This would imply absence of infinite components at $p=1/2$ for several classes of planar graphs, including recurrent simple plane triangulations and suitable Benjamini–Schramm limits. It remains open even for triangulation circle packings with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$ and uniformly bounded disk radii.
source_name: Ron Peled, “On the site percolation threshold of circle packings and planar graphs”, arXiv:2001.10855 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10855

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2020). “It is pointed out in that the conjecture is open even when the probability to color a square black is $2/3$, and to the author's knowledge the conjecture is open for all fixed probabilities in $[1/2,1)$.”
